transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-31
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Recording: fireflies/recordings/ff-20261031-harvestai-01.mp3
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (CTO, HarvestAI), Daniel Rivera (Lead ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Security)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be brief): Discussed quickstart credits, TTFT expectations for a small prototype, options for VPC/private deployment for PII dataset, and next steps for pilot benchmarks.

[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Lina, I'm the AE for Redwood Inference. Marcus is our solutions engineer. Can we do quick intros?
[00:09] Asha Patel: Hi, I'm Asha, CTO at HarvestAI, we build crop analytics, we're exploring adding LLM features into field reports and user Q&A. Daniel is our lead on infra for ML, and Priya runs security.
[00:22] Marcus Chen: Hey all, nice to meet you. Quick note on my side, we'll try to cover time-to-first-token and what a quickstart pilot would look like.
[00:30] Daniel Rivera: Cool. High level, we want something that moves fast — ideally self-serve credits, get to a small prototype in under a week. But we also have constraints around data residency and encryption.
[00:42] Priya Kapoor: And SOC2 + SSO are blockers for anything going into production. We also need clarity on KMS integrations and whether logs can be redacted.
[00:52] Lina Park: Totally. That's what we'll focus on. For HarvestAI's quickstart, we typically offer an initial credit pack for PLG signups — that gets you to first token and a prototype. After that you can decide hosted, dedicated, or private.
[01:06] Asha Patel: Can you remind me the differences? We read the docs but wanted the tradeoffs explained in plain terms — latency vs cost vs data control.
[01:14] Marcus Chen: Sure. Hosted is fastest time-to-value: Redwood-hosted control plane, you call the API, we manage infra. Best for iteration. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for consistent throughput and lower variance in latency — it's a contract. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you isolation and control — good when compliance or data residency require it, but it takes longer to stand up.
[01:39] Daniel Rivera: For our use case — lots of small requests from field agents, 95th p99 latency matter — we'd like 200-300ms p95 for short prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?
[01:50] Marcus Chen: It depends on model and prompt length. For smaller open models in 8-bit quant, you can get single-token latencies that are low, but end-to-end is also network. Hosted in a nearby region usually hits sub-300ms for short prompts on our fast-profile models. If you want strict p95 p99 SLAs, Dedicated is the safer path because you can reserve capacity and avoid noisy neighbors.
[02:12] Asha Patel: And what about KV cache — will session contexts be kept in our control? We don't want sensitive context logged.
[02:20] Lina Park: By default we have prefix/KV caching to speed up repeat requests, but you can opt out. For private deployments or VPC, you control the KV store. For hosted we offer configs around retention and redaction; Marcus can share the security doc.
[02:33] Priya Kapoor: Ok please send the security pack. Also need to know if we can bring our own KMS for key management.
[02:40] Marcus Chen: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we have KMS integrations (customer-managed keys). Hosted can also integrate with customer KMS via a managed HSM option in most cases — I'll detail that.
[02:50] Daniel Rivera: About quickstart credits — what's typical? We want enough to run a meaningful benchmark: ~100k tokens? Also want to try streaming responses.
[02:58] Lina Park: Our PLG credit packs are flexible. We can issue credits and a small sandbox account that unlocks streaming. For a 100k token benchmark that's usually covered by the starter credit. We'll attach a playbook on how to run the TTFT path.
[03:12] Asha Patel: Great. How long does it take for a new account to hit first token if our dev starts today?
[03:18] Marcus Chen: If you do self-serve sign-up it's often minutes to get API keys. With our quickstart templates, a simple app can call in under an hour. If you want Redwood-hosted but with VPC connections or private link, that adds networking steps and may take a few days.
[03:32] Lina Park: For most PLG customers we see TTFT (time-to-first-token) within the same day, often under an hour with basic integration.
[03:39] Daniel Rivera: Sounds good. We might want to try hosted first to validate latency/cost, then move to dedicated if throughput or SLOs require it. Is fallback between variants easy?
[03:49] Marcus Chen: Yes, our smart routing and model variants let you fallback to a cheaper/compatible variant if capacity is constrained. Rollouts and A/B testing are supported in the console, so you can test on hosted and later pin to dedicated builds.
[04:03] Priya Kapoor: What about audit logs? We need full request traces for our SOC2 audit and redaction capabilities for PII.
[04:11] Lina Park: We provide request-level logs, latency breakdowns, and optional persistence windows. For PII we have automatic redaction and can configure streaming not to persist certain payload fields. I'll include the exact retention controls in the security pack.
[04:25] Asha Patel: On pricing — is dedicated a flat monthly cost plus usage or fully reserved?
[04:31] Lina Park: Typically reserved capacity contracts are monthly or annual commits plus an overage rate if you burst. Dedicated reduces per-token variability and often lowers unit costs at scale. We'll include a sample TCO sheet for your expected qps and prompt sizes.
[04:45] Daniel Rivera: For the benchmark, we want to replicate our real traffic: ~10 qps average, spikes to 80 qps over brief windows, prompt size average 350 tokens, sometimes up to 1k. Can Redwood simulate that?
[04:58] Marcus Chen: We can provide a benchmark harness and an example load profile. For the pilot we'd ask you to send a sanitized sample of payloads so we can run parallel tests on hosted and a dedicated pool to compare latency/cost.
[05:12] Asha Patel: Ok I'll coordinate that.
[05:16] Mike (unclear): Quick question, is there support for function calling/structured output? We need JSON outputs for downstream pipelines.
[05:23] Marcus Chen: Yes, we support function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs. For the models we surface stable structured output and we can help set up schema validation in the evals.
[05:35] Priya Kapoor: One more compliance question — we operate partially in EU. Data residency?
[05:40] Lina Park: We have region options for hosted deployments in EU regions; Private or Dedicated in an EU cloud or on-prem is also possible for strict residency. We'll flag region options in the deck.
[05:52] Daniel Rivera: Any gotchas around model compatibility or SDKs? We're using Python + Node.
[05:58] Marcus Chen: Our SDKs support Python and Node and the REST API is straightforward. Model onboarding is simple for common model formats; if you have a custom quantized artifact we can talk through the compatibility. Note sometimes callbacks like stream chunking differ by runtime — we'll share code samples.
[06:18] Asha Patel: Regarding telemetry - will we see token-level costs broken down? We need to map feature cost to our product metrics.
[06:25] Lina Park: Yes, the console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model. We also have tracing hooks for request attribution.
[06:33] Daniel Rivera: Can we bring our own model weights for private? We may want a proprietary LLM for specific tasks.
[06:38] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. Private deployments support customer-owned model artifacts; we have a process for onboarding and verifying performance. For Dedicated we can host your model artifacts too with isolation.
[06:50] Asha Patel: Cool. I want to make sure our quick experiment doesn't leak any PII. What's the recommended best practice for prototyping with sensitive data?
[06:57] Priya Kapoor: Right — we usually sanitize, token-mask PII, or use synthetic datasets. Also test in private or dedicated if you need guaranteed isolation.
[07:07] Lina Park: Agreed — initially we recommend a sanitized subset in hosted or a private sandbox for heavy PII. We'll include the recommended TTFT playbook which outlines sanitization steps and sample cURL/SDK commands.
[07:21] Daniel Rivera: What about SSO for the console? We need SAML/SCIM for team provisioning.
[07:27] Marcus Chen: We support SAML-based SSO and SCIM for provisioning in enterprise tiers. For PLG signups you can invite team members; for Dedicated/Private we typically set up SSO during onboarding.
[07:38] Asha Patel: Can you run a short demo or show the console quickly?
[07:42] Lina Park: We can do a live lighter demo — Marcus, want to share screen for a quick run?
[07:45] Marcus Chen: Sure, I'll walk through the console flow and the quickstart. (screen share noise)
[07:50] [screen share noise and short pause]
[08:10] Marcus Chen: Ok on my screen — this is the sandbox account creation flow, here's where you add API keys, here's the quickstart template for streaming chat, and here's the credits balance shown in the billing tab. You can also enable streaming and toggle retention for logs here.
[08:30] Asha Patel: Nice, is the credits usage per-project? We want separate projects per team.
[08:35] Marcus Chen: Yes projects and per-token attribution exist. You can create multiple API keys per project.
[08:42] Daniel Rivera: That visualization helps. For the bench, can you show how to pin a model variant?
[08:47] Marcus Chen: In the model routing tab you can pin a route to a model id and set rollout percentage. That drives which backend serving profile is used — e.g., fast vs cost-optimized.
[08:58] Asha Patel: OK good.
[09:01] Mike: Any known limitations with streaming and mobile clients? We're doing some field mobile apps.
[09:07] Marcus Chen: Mobile streaming is supported; network variance can increase latency so it's a good reason to test in hosted first. For mobile, smaller chunk sizes and lower context lengths help.
[09:18] Asha Patel: We're reasonably convinced. What immediate steps do you recommend for TTFT pilot?
[09:24] Lina Park: Short list: 1) We'll create a sandbox account and apply starter credits. 2) Marcus sends a benchmark plan and harness. 3) HarvestAI shares sanitized sample payloads and traffic profile. 4) We run hosted benchmark and compare to a small dedicated pool if you want.
[09:39] Daniel Rivera: Timeline? We want to run bench next week if possible.
[09:43] Marcus Chen: We can have the harness and instructions in 3 business days. If you send payloads by end of week, we can run baseline hosted tests next week.
[09:53] Priya Kapoor: I'll send the compliance list we need to see before we open any prod keys.
[09:58] Lina Park: Great. I'll follow up with pricing, credits, and the security pack after this call.
[10:04] Asha Patel: Any risks or gotchas we should be aware of?
[10:08] Marcus Chen: Minor: if you're using extremes of prompt length, kernel selection and memory use can change throughput. Also watch out for KV cache warmup when you move to dedicated — cache hit patterns can change performance. We'll include tips.
[10:22] Daniel Rivera: Understood. For the benchmark we'd like both latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[10:28] Lina Park: We'll deliver a sample TCO with that metric.
[10:32] Asha Patel: Ok, sounds good. Happy to move forward.
[10:35] Lina Park: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll send the deck and security pack. Marcus will propose the bench plan. Any last questions?
[10:43] Mike: No, thanks.
[10:45] Priya Kapoor: One quick thing — is there a data deletion SLA?
[10:49] Lina Park: Yes, we document deletion APIs and retention windows in the security pack; for private you can enforce immediate deletion. I'll include that.
[10:58] Asha Patel: Thanks all.
[11:01] Lina Park: Thanks — we'll follow up.

(End of transcript; timestamps approximate)
